description:
pkix-lint/src/oscal/emit.rs:99:

    pub fn assessment_results(report: &EvaluationReport) -> Value;

    pub fn risks_from_store(store: &DeviationStore) -> Vec<Value>;

    pub fn deviation_store_from_risks(value: &Value) -> Result<DeviationStore, ParseError>;

    pub fn resolve_profile(profile: &Value, sources: &HashMap<String, Value>)
        -> Result<ResolvedProfile, ParseError>;

The OSCAL public surface is entirely `serde_json::Value` in / out. This
is intentional — the OSCAL spec is JSON, and there's no point in
constructing typed mirrors for the entire OSCAL Assessment-Results
schema. But it locks pkix-lint's OSCAL API to serde_json's major
version forever.

If serde_json cuts 2.0 (e.g., Value gains a new variant or changes
Number representation), pkix-lint must cut a major bump too, even
when the OSCAL semantics haven't changed.

# What the caller cannot do

A caller using `pkix-lint = { version = \"0.x\", features = [\"oscal\"] }`
will receive whatever serde_json version pkix-lint's workspace pin
selects. They cannot pin pkix-lint and float serde_json independently
because the types appear in pkix-lint's public function signatures.

# Mitigations

1. Document the version-coupling on the oscal module (similar to
   PKIX-hy2e.23 for pkix-path re-exports).

2. Wrap serde_json::Value in a newtype that delegates serialization
   — but that's lots of code for marginal benefit.

3. Pin serde_json as a workspace-level `1.0.*` and treat any future
   serde_json 2.0 as a coordinated workspace event. This is the
   pragmatic choice — serde_json's 1.x line has been stable since
   2018 with no concrete major-bump signal.

# Why P3

serde_json is the de facto stable point in the Rust ecosystem. The
risk is real but the probability is low. Document it explicitly so
the contract is honest, and don't pretend the version-decoupling
exists when it doesn't.

# Suggested fix

Add a # Stability section to the oscal module rustdoc:

    /// # serde_json version coupling
    ///
    /// The public OSCAL API uses serde_json::Value directly. A major
    /// version bump in serde_json (currently 1.x) would force a major
    /// bump in pkix-lint. We do not wrap Value behind a newtype to
    /// avoid carrying duplicate JSON modeling code; if serde_json 2.0
    /// happens, this crate will cut its own 2.0 as a coordinated
    /// workspace release.
title: API contract: oscal::emit::assessment_results returns serde_json::Value, ties caller to serde_json major
